title: Reconstructing an equivariant homogeneous-function lift from a tensor map
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative condensed ring on the small coherent profinite site [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, def-weil-size-convention], and let $G$ be a profinite group, with $\underline G(S)=C(S,G)$. Use internal $A$-modules, internal $G$-actions, their forgetful functor $U$, and section modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-condensed-action-module, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For a profinite parameter $X$, let $A[\underline X]$ be the free internal module, left adjoint to forgetting to condensed sets, with canonical local generators $[t]$ [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data, def-sfb-condensed-free-module-generators]. Use internal tensor and its right-adjoint internal Hom [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], whose sections are maps on the entire slice [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Fix $n\geq0$ and an equivariant module $J$. Put $P_n=A[\underline G^n]$, with $G^0=*$, and $\mathcal H_n(J)=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_A(A[\underline G^{n+1}],UJ)$. A normalized homogeneous-function model means an equivariant module identified underneath with $\mathcal H_n(J)$ and having action $(k\cdot f)(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=k\cdot_J f(k^{-1}g_0,\ldots,k^{-1}g_n)$ on every profinite slice [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions].
The displayed homogeneous action admits a normalized homogeneous-function model $H$. For every such model, every equivariant module $M$, and every internal $A$-linear map $\beta:P_n\otimes_A UM\to UJ$, the following formula defines an equivariant internal $A$-linear morphism $b_\beta:M\to H$:
$$b_\beta(m)(g_0,\ldots,g_n)=g_0\cdot_J\beta\bigl([g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_0^{-1}g_n]\otimes(g_0^{-1}\cdot_M m)\bigr).$$
Precisely, for every $S$, $m\in M(S)$, base change $T\to S$, and $g_i\in C(T,G)$, the left side is the slice evaluation of $b_{\beta,S}(m)$, and the right side uses $m|_T$ and $\beta_T$. In particular $b_\beta(m)(1,\mathbf t)=\beta([\mathbf t]\otimes m)$ on every slice. If $N$ is any equivariant module, $i:N\to M$ and $h:N\to H$ are equivariant internal linear maps, and
$$\beta([\mathbf t]\otimes i(x))=h(x)(1,\mathbf t)$$
on every profinite test and after every base change, then $b_\beta\circ i=h$. This assertion assumes neither monicity of $i$ nor injectivity of $UJ$. It includes $n=0$, the trivial group, the empty test object, and zero coefficients.

proof.text: Use the following immediate combination of the cited universal properties. If $X$ is a condensed set, $V,W$ are internal modules, and $F_T(x,v)\in W(T)$ is natural in every profinite $T$, for $x\in X(T),v\in V(T)$, and $A(T)$-linear in $v$, then it determines a unique map $A[X]\otimes_A V\to W$ with value $F_T(x,v)$ on $[x]\otimes v$. Indeed for $x\in X(S)$ the maps $v\mapsto F_T(x|_T,v)$ for every $T\to S$ are a morphism $V|_S\to W|_S$, hence a section of the slice sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. These sections are natural in $S,x$. The free-generator bijection [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor] extends them uniquely to $A[X]\to\mathcal Hom_A(V,W)$; uncurrying by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], using its symmetry, gives the asserted map and formula. Conversely its curry recovers the same sections. Thus equality of these maps is detected on the indicated generators and arbitrary local $v$; equality of their transposes is detected by those same slice evaluations. This argument makes no claim that sections of a sheafified free module are themselves finite free sums. In particular, for the representable parameter $Q=G^{n+1}$, the section description in [def-sfb-condensed-equivariant-bar-data] identifies an element of $\mathcal Hom_A(A[Q],UJ)(S)$ with its entire natural family of evaluations on $T\to S$ and $q:T\to Q$. It therefore detects equality of these sections, including every action-law calculation below.

source.place: Paragraph (3), open-direct-image helper: explicit free-generator and tensor–Hom construction; supporting Stacks Tag 03EO, lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor (2).

proof.text: Put $Q=\underline G^{n+1}$ and $K=\mathcal Hom_A(A[Q],UJ)$. For every test $T$, $(k,q)\in(\underline G\times Q)(T)$ and $c\in K(T)$, set $F_T((k,q),c)=k\cdot_J c(k^{-1}q)$, where $k^{-1}q=(k^{-1}q_0,\ldots,k^{-1}q_n)$. Slice evaluation is linear in $c$, and $k\cdot_J-$ is $A(T)$-linear [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. The expression commutes with restriction because evaluation and the action do. Step 1 gives $A[\underline G\times Q]\otimes_A K\to UJ$. The free-product tensor isomorphism of [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor], associativity and symmetry rewrite its source as $A[Q]\otimes_A(A[\underline G]\otimes_A K)$. Curry with [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] to obtain $A[\underline G]\otimes_A K\to K$. On $[k]\otimes c$ it has slice evaluation $q\mapsto k\cdot_J c(k^{-1}q)$. Composing the free-generator map in the first variable defines a natural action of the condensed set $\underline G$ on $K$, linear in $c$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), homogeneous-function helper: construct the displayed action on the internal Hom, rather than assume its existence.

proof.text:
For $k,l\in C(S,G)$ and $c\in K(S)$, evaluate after every $T\to S$ at $q\in Q(T)$, writing $k,l$ for their restrictions. The action of step 2 satisfies
$$(k\cdot(l\cdot c))(q)=k\cdot_J\bigl(l\cdot_J c(l^{-1}k^{-1}q)\bigr)=(kl)\cdot_J c((kl)^{-1}q)=((kl)\cdot c)(q),$$
and $(1\cdot c)(q)=c(q)$. The action laws of $J$ give these equalities without any commutativity assumption on $G$. Step 1's generator detection, or equivalently the free-generator bijection on each of the slice evaluations, makes them equalities of sections of $K$. Thus the natural linear operations form the homomorphisms required by [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. With underlying module $K$ and identity identification, they give a normalized homogeneous-function model as specified in [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions].

source.place: Paragraph (3), homogeneous-function helper: identity and multiplication laws on all slices.

proof.text:
Now fix $\beta$ and first construct its lift into this model. For $q=(g_0,\ldots,g_n)\in Q(T)$ and $m\in M(T)$ put
$$B_T(q,m)=g_0\cdot_J\beta_T\bigl([g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_0^{-1}g_n]\otimes(g_0^{-1}\cdot_M m)\bigr).$$
This is $A(T)$-linear in $m$, since both group actions are linear and $\beta$ is linear. It is natural in $T$: restriction commutes separately with inversion and multiplication of continuous group-valued maps, the free-adjunction unit, the tensor pairing, both actions and $\beta$. Step 1 therefore supplies a genuine internal map $A[Q]\otimes_A UM\to UJ$. Its transpose is $b_\beta:UM\to K$ by [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], with exactly the stated evaluation formula at every $T\to S$, applied to $m|_T$. For an arbitrary normalized model $H$, compose with the inverse of its underlying-module identification with $K$; the action formula defining that model [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions] is unchanged under this identification. Hence the same construction and all subsequent calculations apply to every such $H$.

source.place: Paragraph (3), old reconstruction step: construct the slice-natural linear lift by free linearization and tensor–Hom adjunction.

proof.text:
Check equivariance on every slice. For $k\in C(S,G)$, restrict to $T\to S$, put $q=(g_0,\ldots,g_n)\in Q(T)$, and abbreviate $r=(g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_0^{-1}g_n)$. Using the normalized action on $H$,
$$\begin{aligned}(k\cdot_H b_\beta(m))(q)&=k\cdot_J b_\beta(m)(k^{-1}g_0,\ldots,k^{-1}g_n)\\&=k\cdot_J\bigl((k^{-1}g_0)\cdot_J\beta_T([r]\otimes((g_0^{-1}k)\cdot_M m))\bigr)\\&=g_0\cdot_J\beta_T([r]\otimes(g_0^{-1}\cdot_M(k\cdot_M m)))\\&=b_\beta(k\cdot_M m)(q).\end{aligned}$$
Here $(k^{-1}g_0)^{-1}(k^{-1}g_i)=g_0^{-1}g_i$; the two action laws give the next equality. Detection by all slice evaluations from step 1 proves equality in $H(S)$. Thus the internal linear map from step 4 is equivariant in the precise sense of [def-sfb-condensed-action-module]. No equivariance of $\beta$ is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), old equivariance step: explicit cancellation calculation on arbitrary profinite base change.

proof.text:
Putting $g_0=1$ and $(g_1,\ldots,g_n)=\mathbf t$ in step 4 gives $b_\beta(m)(1,\mathbf t)=\beta([\mathbf t]\otimes m)$ on every slice. For the extension assertion, fix $x\in N(S)$ and evaluate after any $T\to S$ at $q=(g_0,\ldots,g_n)$. Write $x$ for its restriction and $r=(g_0^{-1}g_1,\ldots,g_0^{-1}g_n)$. Equivariance of $i$, followed by the assumed identity with $g_0^{-1}\cdot_N x$ as input, gives
$$b_\beta(i(x))(q)=g_0\cdot_J\beta_T([r]\otimes i(g_0^{-1}\cdot_N x))=g_0\cdot_J h(g_0^{-1}\cdot_N x)(1,r).$$
Equivariance of $h$ identifies the last expression with $g_0\cdot_J(g_0^{-1}\cdot_H h(x))(1,r)$. The normalized action formula [def-sfb-condensed-homogeneous-functions] makes this $g_0\cdot_J(g_0^{-1}\cdot_J h(x)(g_0,g_0r))=h(x)(q)$. Step 1's detection proves $b_\beta\circ i=h$. This uses neither cancellation of $i$ nor extension by injectivity.

source.place: Paragraph (3), old extension-identity step: use the prescribed identity on $g_0^{-1}x$ and write out both equivariance substitutions.

proof.text: All powers are finite products; at $n=0$, $r$ is the unique empty tuple and $A[\underline G^0]=A[1]\cong A$ by [lem-sfb-condensed-free-linearization-tensor]. The formulas then read $b_\beta(m)(g_0)=g_0\cdot_J\beta([*]\otimes g_0^{-1}\cdot_M m)$ and the same cancellation calculations apply. For the trivial group every action is the identity and the lift is the transpose of $\beta$ at the terminal parameter. Over the empty test object every module sheaf has a singleton set of sections, so all identities hold; zero coefficients force every unital module section to be zero. None of the construction or calculations discards these cases.

lean.statement: theorem homogeneous_lift_reconstruction (J : ActionModule R G) (n : ℕ) : Nonempty (HomogeneousFunctions R G J n) ∧ ∀ (H : HomogeneousFunctions R G J n) (M : ActionModule R G) (β : InternalBar.freePower R G n ⊗ M.module ⟶ J.module), ∃ b : M ⟶ H.object, (∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (m : sectionModule R M.module S) (T : Profinite.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (q : Fin (n + 1) → C(T, G)), homogeneousEvaluate R G J n S ((H.internalHom.hom.val.app (op S)).hom (InternalBar.onSections R b.val S m)) T f q = J.act T (q 0) (InternalBar.onSections R β T (InternalBar.pureTensor R (InternalBar.freePower R G n) M.module T (InternalBar.generator R G n T (fun i ↦ (q 0)⁻¹ * q i.succ)) (M.act T (q 0)⁻¹ ((M.module.X.obj.map f.op).hom m))))) ∧ (∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (m : sectionModule R M.module S) (T : Profinite.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (t : Fin n → C(T, G)), homogeneousEvaluate R G J n S ((H.internalHom.hom.val.app (op S)).hom (InternalBar.onSections R b.val S m)) T f (Fin.cons 1 t) = InternalBar.onSections R β T (InternalBar.pureTensor R (InternalBar.freePower R G n) M.module T (InternalBar.generator R G n T t) ((M.module.X.obj.map f.op).hom m))) ∧ (∀ (N : ActionModule R G) (i : N ⟶ M) (h : N ⟶ H.object), (∀ (S : Profinite.{u}) (x : sectionModule R N.module S) (T : Profinite.{u}) (f : T ⟶ S) (t : Fin n → C(T, G)), InternalBar.onSections R β T (InternalBar.pureTensor R (InternalBar.freePower R G n) M.module T (InternalBar.generator R G n T t) (InternalBar.onSections R i.val T ((N.module.X.obj.map f.op).hom x))) = homogeneousEvaluate R G J n S ((H.internalHom.hom.val.app (op S)).hom (InternalBar.onSections R h.val S x)) T f (Fin.cons 1 t)) → i ≫ b = h)
